Issue 6727 asks for HLSL intrinsics exposing the two outputs of the DXIL
IMul/UMul/UDiv operations. The source below is the smallest case: the quotient
and the remainder of one operand pair.

FXC pane (cs_5_0, DXBC): a single udiv instruction, writing quotient and
remainder into two destination registers from one divide.

DXC panes (cs_6_0, DXIL): two independent instructions, a udiv and a urem, and
no dx.op call for either.

DXIL does define two-output forms of these operations, as opcodes 41, 42 and 43,
and DXC's own DXBC-to-DXIL converter emits them. Nothing in the HLSL front end
does, which is what this issue is asking for.

Careful when searching the DXC panes: Compiler Explorer compiles with debug info,
so this banner is embedded verbatim in the shader's own !dx.source.contents
metadata. Any operation name written here would be findable in the pane text
without the compiler having emitted anything of the sort. That is why the op
class name is not spelled out above; see the issue comment for it.

The multiply half of the request is absent from this file because FXC has no
64-bit integers. In DXC the high 32 bits of a 32x32 multiply can only be reached
by widening to uint64_t, which adds the optional 64-bit integer feature to the
shader.
